Hi Sophie,

Thanks for raising this — sorry for the confusion. I have looped in Vivek from Finance to confirm treatment. If your DE VAT ID validates as a German B2B VAT registration and the supply is treated as cross-border B2B services, we typically apply reverse-charge (i.e., we should not charge German VAT).

Could you please send a copy of the VAT certificate or the exact VAT number verification screenshot? We will validate it in VIES and reissue the invoice with the correct tax language and zero-rated VAT if appropriate.

I've attached our quick VAT information request form to capture the details we need. If you prefer, a signed header on company letterhead works as well.

Next steps:
- Sophie: provide VAT evidence (certificate or VIES screenshot)
- Finance (Vivek): validate in VIES and confirm reverse-charge eligibility
- Naomi: reissue corrected invoice and send payment instructions

Apologies for the extra step — we'll prioritize this so your AP team can process payment.

Thanks,

Naomi / Priyom,

I validated the VAT number DE123456789 in VIES — status: active (lookup timestamp 2026-02-19T11:40Z). Since EuRetailers GmbH is a German-registered business and our supply is a cross-border B2B digital service, the correct treatment is reverse-charge. That means:

- Do NOT charge German VAT on the invoice (remove VAT line).
- Include the buyer VAT number on the invoice (DE123456789).
- Supplier tax note: "VAT reverse-charged — Article 196 of Council Directive 2006/112/EC. Recipient to account for VAT."
- Keep the same net amount and payment terms (Net 30).

Please reissue INV-2026-029 as a corrected invoice (INV-2026-029-corrected.pdf) with the above language and resend to Sophie / accounts. I'll file a short internal memo for our records and attach the VIES lookup screenshot to the transaction for audit.

Vivek
Head of Finance | Redwood Inference

[internal note: confirm that US tax counsel has no exceptions; none flagged in prior reviews for EU B2B SaaS reverse-charge]
